newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: GCC welcomes new Iran policies, slam Iraq, Israel.
newsitem.headline: GCC welcomes new Iran policies, slam Iraq, Israel.

text.p: Gulf Arab foreign ministers on Wednesday welcomed Iranian attempts to improve ties with their countries but criticised the policies of Iraq and Israel.
The foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait repeated calls for Iran to end its occupation of three Gulf islands claimed by the UAE.

But in a statement issued at the end of talks in Riyadh, they welcomed recent Iranian attempts to mend fences with the six-nation Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) based on "mutual trust, respect, confidence, non-aggression and non-interference in each other's internal affairs".

Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati toured the six oil-rich Gulf states this month and said the visits helped open a new chapter in relations. Days later, Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Abdullah met at an Islamic summit in Islamabad.

"The GCC council welcomes the new Iranian outlook as expressed by Dr Velayati during the tour and the assurances carried by the Iranian leadership in its recent contacts with GCC states," the statement said.
"They also express willingness to respond to the Iranian outlook and assurances and to work to build confidence and put Iranian-GCC ties on the right track politically and media-wise."
Some Gulf Arab states have accused Iran of interfering in their internal affairs -- a charge Iran denies -- and have voiced concern over its arms buildup. Iran says its arms programme is defensive.
Regarding other regional issues, the six ministers blamed rising tension in the West Bank on Israeli plans to build a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
They welcomed the implementation of an oil-for-food deal signed between Iraq and the United Nations last year.

But they blamed the Iraqi leadership for the Iraqi people's continued suffering and urged Baghdad to adhere to U.N. Gulf War ceasefire resolutions which call among other things for freeing 600 Kuwaiti prisoners of war and cooperating with U.N. disarmament efforts.
Iraq became the Gulf Arabs' enemy in 1990 when it invaded Kuwait. It was driven from Kuwait in the 1991 Gulf War.
